entry.title: Pressing, sticking, rolling
entry.summary: Davies describes glue, clay, and play dough as chances to explore how materials change. These are shared, supervised explorations, with no model to copy.
entry.cue: Notice an interest in pressing shapes down or changing a material with the hands.
detail: Her gluing example uses paper shapes with a small pot of glue and brush, or a glue stick. The movement is to apply glue, turn the shape, and press it onto paper; the appendix uses a few large shapes.

For clay or play dough, she describes flattening, rolling, making a ball, and trying simple tools. She also names kinetic sand as another material experience. Small parts and sharp tools require supervision.
The activity is the experimenting. A child may repeat one movement and leave the rest for another time.
